clue.text: Norman qualifies — a triumph!

parts.note: surface reading: a man called Norman passes his exams
setter's reading: the word Norman is the qualifier placed before a word for a triumph, naming the events of 1066

explanation.surface: Someone called Norman has passed his exams, and it is celebrated as a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norman Conquest was William of Normandy's invasion of England in 1066; 'Norman' qualifies the answer in that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A conquest is a victory gained by force, so it can stand for a triumph or win.

clue.text: State in charge of circle manufacturing cloth

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California
i/c is the standard abbreviation for in charge
a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A US state is in charge of a group of textile manufacturers.
explanation.definitionFit: Calico is a plain-woven cotton fabric, originally from Calicut in India.

clue.text: One, for example, that's more insensitive

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a numeral, of which one is an instance
second meaning: the comparative of numb, pronounced differently

explanation.surface: Someone is described as being more unfeeling than the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is pronounced NUM-er, comparing numb, not the counting word.
explanation.definitionFit: One is an example of a numeral, while numb plus -er gives the comparative meaning having less feeling.

clue.text: Purses and fiddle found in tunnel

indicators.note: to fiddle with something is to tinker or tamper, so these letters are moved about

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Stolen purses and evidence of a swindle are discovered in a tunnel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' looks like a noun, a swindle, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An underpass is a road or path running beneath another road, a short tunnel.

clue.text: 100 mph one achieved, after a short time in the lead

parts.note: a second is a brief moment
a ton is slang for a hundred miles an hour
taken as written

explanation.surface: A racer hitting 100 mph takes the lead after a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Doing a ton is British slang for driving at 100 mph; 'after' puts the second piece ahead of those two.
explanation.definitionFit: Second to none is an idiom meaning the very best, beaten by nobody, so in the lead.

clue.text: Accountant's menu varied with insight

indicators.note: something varied has been changed about, so the letters of the menu are rearranged

parts.note: AC is an abbreviation for accountant; the 's means 'has'
the letters of menu rearranged

explanation.surface: An accountant has altered the menu, showing business insight.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is shrewd judgement, the ability to see clearly into a situation, which is insight.

clue.text: Abrupt, accepting nothing from Council

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: curt means abrupt in manner
O is a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone was abrupt in accepting nothing from the local council.
explanation.definitionFit: A court is a monarch's council of advisers, and the word also names assemblies that govern or judge.

clue.text: The small hours might be interrupted by strange din

indicators.note: something interrupted has another thing pushed into its middle

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of din rearranged

explanation.surface: Sleep in the small hours might be broken by a strange noise.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled din goes after the first two letters of might.
explanation.definitionFit: Midnight marks the start of the small hours, the time just after twelve at night.

clue.text: Reporter giving fresh information to young woman

parts.note: news is fresh information
a girl is a young woman

explanation.surface: A journalist passes on the latest information to a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsgirl is a girl who sells or delivers newspapers, or informally a female reporter of news.

clue.text: Nothing gained after disabled leader left powerless

parts.note: lame means unable to walk properly
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket

explanation.surface: A disabled leader, deprived of power, has achieved nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter out without scoring makes a duck, so duck means nothing; 'after' puts it behind the word for disabled.
explanation.definitionFit: A lame duck is an official, typically a president, still in office but without real power after a successor is chosen.

clue.text: Son expected sound plant

indicators.note: sound tells us to go by how the preceding words are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: son is pronounced the same as sun
due, meaning expected, is pronounced like dew

explanation.surface: A son was expected to grow up a sound, healthy plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The sundew is a small carnivorous bog plant that traps insects on sticky glistening hairs.

clue.text: Suspect, one in arms dealing, taken aside

indicators.note: as a verb-turned-adjective suspect means dubious, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suspect, one of those involved in illegal arms dealing, is taken aside for questioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' looks like a noun, a person under suspicion, but it signals the anagram of the next words.
explanation.definitionFit: To be marginalised is to be pushed to the edges and treated as unimportant, set apart from the mainstream.

clue.text: New cartel took time out, then focussed

indicators.note: something new has been made afresh, so the letters are given a fresh order
taking something out means removing it, and time stands for its usual one-letter abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time, removed here

explanation.surface: A newly formed cartel took a break and then concentrated on business.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the T from cartel and rearrange the remaining five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An image that is focussed is sharp and distinct, which is what clear describes.

clue.text: Close shave for adjacent object

definitions.meaning: second meaning, taken literally: an item that is nearby

explanation.surface: A close shave from a razor, with the object of the shave sitting nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape from disaster is idiomatically called a near thing, and read literally the phrase means a nearby item.

clue.text: Farm vehicle to go back for Rocky Harper, the surveyor

parts.note: a cart is a farm vehicle

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word is read right to left
rocky means unsteady, so the letters of the name wobble into a new order

parts.note: go written backwards
the letters of Harper rearranged

explanation.surface: A farm cart has to be sent back for someone called Rocky Harper, the land surveyor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' looks like a first name, but it is the anagram signal for Harper.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartographer is a mapmaker, and mapping land involves surveying it.

clue.text: Tee-total seamen dreadfully intent

indicators.note: something done dreadfully is badly done, so these letters are botched into a new order

parts.note: ABs are able seamen
the letters of intent rearranged

explanation.surface: Sailors who are fiercely determined to stay off the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a naval rating; the plural ABS gives the first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstinent means refraining from something, especially alcohol, which is what a teetotaller does.

clue.text: Impotent rage when love apple cooked by two unknowns

indicators.note: cooked means prepared and mixed, and also falsified, so these letters are worked into another order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
taken as written
x and y are the usual unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a futile fury when the tomato is cooked by two strangers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love apple' is an old name for the tomato, but here love and apple are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Apoplexy is a stroke, and figuratively a fit of extreme anger that leaves one speechless.

clue.text: About another spiral in an act of vengeance

indicators.note: another version is a different form, so the letters take a new shape

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the letters of spiral rearranged

explanation.surface: Talk of another downward spiral of violence, each act taken in revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is retaliation against an enemy for harm done, a deed of revenge.

clue.text: Delightful quality of picturesque headland

parts.note: a picturesque place is pleasant to look at
a ness is a headland or promontory

explanation.surface: Praising the delightful character of a scenic headland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ness is a British word for a headland, found in place names such as Dungeness in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasantness is the state of being agreeable, a noun naming a delightful quality.

clue.text: Church elevation in colour

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a rise is an elevation or high ground

explanation.surface: A church on high ground is painted in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerise is a deep cherry-red shade, named from the French for cherry.

clue.text: Way of knowing every signal initially that adds fuel to the flames

parts.note: St is short for street

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each word is used

parts.note: the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A way of recognising every warning sign that makes a fire worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' looks like a link word, but its initial is needed too.
explanation.definitionFit: To stoke a fire is to feed it with fuel, so stokes is what one does who adds fuel.

clue.text: Son occupied vacant ruin in island town with staff

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to sit inside it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Peel is a town on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: in places what comes before it inside the next piece
a vacant word has been emptied of its contents, keeping only its outside edges

parts.note: the first and last letters of ruin
taken as written

explanation.surface: A son moved into a derelict ruin in an island town and took on staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Son goes inside the outer letters of ruin, and the result goes inside Peel, a town on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Personnel are the people employed by an organisation, its staff.

clue.text: Perform better when not in the party

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone does better when they are excluded from the party.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to surpass or exceed them in performance.

clue.text: Still fashionable with monarch and model

parts.note: something in is in fashion
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
the Model T Ford

explanation.surface: Fashion still involves the monarch and a model.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the late Queen's royal cipher; T comes from the Model T, Ford's famous early car.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means motionless or inactive, the adjectival sense of still.

clue.text: Phoney hesitation the day last letterës written

parts.note: er is a sound of hesitation
Sat is the short form of Saturday
the final letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A fake pause in speech on the day the final letter was written.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of the alphabet completes the word; the odd ë in the clue stands for an apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior substitute or imitation, so it means fake or phoney.

clue.text: Star skier sat awkwardly

indicators.note: done awkwardly means clumsily arranged, so the letters fall into a different order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A star skier is sitting down clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' looks like an adjective praising the skier, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is the printed star-shaped symbol, named from the Greek for little star.

clue.text: Cowardly fellow lost his head; young leader brought in

indicators.note: losing one's head means losing what is at the top, so the first letter goes
a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of young
taken as written, before beheading

explanation.surface: A cowardly man lost his nerve when a young leader was brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the F from fellow and put the first letter of young in its place at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is an informal adjective for lacking courage, a colour long associated with cowardice.

clue.text: Leading journalist is roaming in untamed desert

indicators.note: roaming means wandering about, so these letters wander into a new order
untamed means wild, so these letters are let loose and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A senior journalist is wandering lost in a wild desert.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are mixed together into one shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: An editress is a female editor, the person heading a newspaper's journalists.
